title: I Enforced the Piano-Practice-Room Timer on the Teacher Whose Student Overstayed

parts.text: I knocked on room five at 5:02 p.m. and teacher Hana's student was still on our numbered bench. The light said: ONE ROOM. FORTY-FIVE MINUTES. KEY FOLLOWS THE BOOKING. I was thirty, conservatory member, holding a key fob that listed our slot. Hana shrugged. "Teachers are the room." I photographed the light, the booking, and her bag on our stand. Then I asked for the timer log. At 5:10 the desk pinged why Hana's name was on our forty-five. I kept my voice hall-quiet and let the timestamp talk. A light is only a light until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The desk can see Hana's bag on our stand during our booking.

social.video_title: Her student stayed on our numbered bench past the timer — Part 1/2
social.description: Practice room, a teacher on our stand, a forty-five-minute light she posted. I logged the bag. Would you have asked for the timer log?

parts.text: Hana called it a cadence until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the light, and the bag still. The bench went back to our slot. Hana ran her own forty-five and told the next teacher atmosphere was always about phrasing. Phrasing is a word teachers use when a booking exists. Room policy now has a second line: TEACHERS ARE NOT THE ROOM. I keep our fob on a labeled hook. Hana brown-bags her jokes. The hall finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.
